findings.issue: USER_REFERRAL_TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS=3 assumes user-service sees the raw appended X-Forwarded-For chain, which it most likely does not on Kubernetes. Spring Boot detects CloudPlatform.KUBERNETES and, with server.forward-headers-strategy unset (user-service and gateway set nothing; values.yaml sets it only for auth-service), defaults to NATIVE: (1) user-service's Tomcat RemoteIpValve treats the gateway pod (10.x) as internal, sets getRemoteAddr() to the first non-internal entry from the right and rewrites X-Forwarded-For to the entries left of it, so ClientIp counts hops in an already-shortened, caller-controlled remainder; (2) on the gateway, Reactor Netty sets getRemoteAddress() to the leftmost (forged) entry and XForwardedHeadersFilter appends that forged value. Round-1 bypass, oracle and row-growth paths stay open on AWS; edge-IP fallback can also cause wrong refusals. Compose is unaffected. MockMvc tests never run the Tomcat valve.
findings.fix: Set server.forward-headers-strategy: ${USER_FORWARD_HEADERS_STRATEGY:none} in user-service; set SERVER_FORWARD_HEADERS_STRATEGY=none for the gateway in Helm (or document why not) and confirm RateLimitWebFilter's fallback is unaffected; add a RANDOM_PORT embedded-Tomcat test with spring.main.cloud-platform=kubernetes sending 'spoofed, real-client, edge, alb' from a loopback peer and asserting real-client is recorded. Keep the explicit 'none' as a guard even if Boot 4 no longer defaults to NATIVE.

findings.issue: Short (< 32 bytes) salt only WARNs and a blank salt still starts in prod; accepted and tracked as TD-P8-24.
findings.fix: Under TD-P8-24: fail the prod start on a blank or short salt; wire the secret via Helm secretEnv.

summary: Request changes. Round-1 leftmost-XFF major is fixed in code and for Compose, but not yet effective on AWS: Spring Boot's Kubernetes default forward-headers-strategy (NATIVE) most likely makes Tomcat's RemoteIpValve rewrite X-Forwarded-For before ClientIp reads it, and makes the gateway append a forged leftmost value. Fix with an explicit 'none' strategy plus an embedded-server test. Activity cap, resolver-free parsing (ofLiteral + dotted-quad guard), RETURNING (xmax = 0) upsert, authz, SQL parameterisation, PII handling, deletion cleanup and claim race all verified. Distinct-422 oracle and short-salt WARN accepted under TD-P8-24. Client-IP duplication and AuditInterceptor left to backlog B-1.
